title: Differentiate exponential functions
what: You give it an exponential, like $e^{ax}$ or $a^x$. It gives back its **slope** function.
The key idea: $e^{ax}$ keeps its shape when you differentiate. It only picks up the number $a$ from the power as a multiplier.
question: The mass of a sample is $m(t) = 90e^{-0.2t}$ grams, $t$ hours after it is set up. Find the rate at which the mass is changing when $t = 3$. Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

title: Differentiate trig functions (radians)
input: sin ax, cos ax, tan ax
example: sin 4x → 4 cos 4x; tan x → sec² x
what: You give it a sine, cosine or tangent of $ax$. It gives back the slope function.
The key idea: $\sin ax$ becomes $a\cos ax$, and $\cos ax$ becomes $-a\sin ax$. The $a$ always comes out in front, and the angle is in **radians**.
question: Find the slope of the curve $y = 5\sin 2x + 3\cos x$ at the point where $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

title: Apply the product rule
example: x² sin x → 2x sin x + x² cos x
what: You give it two functions multiplied together, $u \cdot v$. It gives back the slope function of the **product**.
The key idea: you cannot differentiate each part and multiply. Instead, differentiate one at a time and add: $u'v + uv'$.
question: Find the values of $x$ for which the slope of $f(x) = x^2e^{3x}$ is zero.

title: Apply the chain rule
what: You give it a function inside a function, $f(g(x))$. It gives back the slope function by working from the **outside** in.
The key idea: differentiate the outer function and leave the inner one as it is, then multiply by the derivative of the inner function.
question: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y = \sqrt{4x^2 + 9}$ at the point where $x = 2$.

title: Differentiate logarithms
what: You give it the log of a function, $\ln f(x)$. It gives back the slope function, $f'(x)$ over $f(x)$.
The key idea: the derivative of a log is the **derivative of the inside**, divided by the inside.
question: Find the slope of the curve $y = \ln(3x^2 + 1)$ at $x = 1$.

title: Differentiate inverse trig functions
what: You give it an inverse trig function of $x/a$, like $\tan^{-1}(x/a)$. It gives back the slope function.
The key idea: the rule for $\tan^{-1}u$ is $u'$ over $1 + u^2$, and the chain rule supplies $u'$.
question: Differentiate $f(x) = \tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{x}{4}\right)$ and find $f'(4)$.

title: Differentiate from first principles
what: You give it a function, $f(x)$. It finds the slope function $f'(x)$ using the limit $\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}$.
The key idea: the slope between two points a distance $h$ apart becomes the slope **at** a point when $h$ shrinks to zero.
question: Differentiate $f(x) = 2x^2 - x + 3$ from first principles.

title: Apply the quotient rule
what: You give it one function divided by another, $u/v$. It gives back the slope function $\dfrac{u'v - uv'}{v^2}$.
The key idea: differentiate the top and the bottom separately, then combine them in the fixed pattern: bottom times the top's slope, minus top times the bottom's slope, all over the bottom squared.
question: Given $g(x) = \dfrac{3x - 2}{x + 4}$, find $g'(1)$.

title: Differentiate a function needing several rules
input: product/quotient of composites of exp, log, trig, powers
what: You give it a function built from several pieces, like $e^{3x}\cos 2x$. It gives back the **derivative**, simplified.
The key idea: spot the outer rule first (product or quotient). Then use the chain rule on each piece inside it.
question: Differentiate $f(x) = e^{3x}\cos 2x$ with respect to $x$. Write the answer in its simplest form.

title: Show a derivative satisfies a given relation
input: y = f(x) + relation in y, y′, y″
what: You give it a function $y$ and an equation that links $y$, $y'$ and $y''$. It **shows** the equation is true.
The key idea: find $y'$ and $y''$, put all three into the left side, and simplify until it equals the right side.
question: Show that $y = xe^{-2x}$ satisfies $y'' + 4y' + 4y = 0$.

title: Calculate percentages and percentage change
what: You give it quantities. It finds a **percentage**, a percentage change, or the original amount.
The key idea: turn the percentage into a **multiplier**. An increase of $8\%$ is $\times 1.08$. To undo it, divide.
question: The price of a bicycle was increased by $8\%$. It now costs €486. Find the original price.

title: Change units (metric, imperial with factors, currency)
what: You give it a quantity and a conversion factor. It gives back the same quantity in **new units**.
The key idea: change one unit at a time. Multiply when the new unit is smaller, divide when it is bigger.
question: A train travels at $72$ km/h. Express its speed in metres per second.

title: Estimate, round and check order of magnitude
what: You give it a calculation. It gives back a quick **estimate**, close to the real answer, that you can do in your head.
The key idea: round every number to one **significant figure** first. Then the sum is easy, and the answer shows if your calculator work is sensible.
question:
A shop sells $19.8$ kg of cheese at $€6.10$ per kg.
(a) Estimate the cost by rounding each number to one significant figure.
(b) Calculate the exact cost.
(c) Is your answer to (b) sensible?

title: Calculate cost/selling price, discount, mark-up and margin
output: profit, mark-up (% of CP), margin (% of SP)
what: You give it a cost price and a selling price. It finds the **profit**, the **mark-up** and the **margin**.
The key idea: profit is selling price minus cost price. Mark-up is that profit as a percentage of the **cost price**. Margin is the same profit as a percentage of the **selling price**.
question: A shop buys a bag for $€45$ and sells it for $€60$. Find (a) the profit, (b) the mark-up as a percentage of the cost price, (c) the margin as a percentage of the selling price.

title: Apply compound interest
what: You give it a starting amount $P$, a yearly rate and a number of years. It gives back the **final value** $F$.
The key idea: each year the amount is multiplied by the same number, $1 + i$. So after $t$ years you multiply $t$ times, which is $F = P(1 + i)^t$.
question: Aoife invests $€7000$ at $2.5\%$ per year compound interest for $3$ years. Find the value of her investment at the end of $3$ years, to the nearest cent.

title: Apply reducing-balance depreciation
what: You give it a starting value $P$, a yearly rate of loss and a number of years. It gives back the **value** $F$ after those years.
The key idea: each year the value is multiplied by the same number, $1 - i$, because the car keeps $100\% - i$ of what it was worth. So $F = P(1 - i)^t$.
question: A van costs $€25\,000$ new. It loses $10\%$ of its value each year. Find the value of the van after $4$ years.

title: Convert between annual and periodic rates (AER/APR)
what: You give it a rate for one period, such as a yearly rate. It gives back the **equivalent** rate for a different period, such as a month.
The key idea: growth multiplies. Twelve months of growth at rate $i$ must give the same result as one year at the annual rate, so $(1+i)^{12} = 1 + \text{annual rate}$.
question: A bank quotes an annual percentage rate (APR) of $3.6\%$. Find the equivalent monthly rate, correct to 3 significant figures.

title: Calculate income tax, USC, PRSI and net pay
input: gross pay, rates, bands, credits, deductions
output: gross tax, net tax, net pay
what: You give it a gross pay, the tax rates and bands, and the tax credits. It gives back the **gross tax**, the **net tax** and the **net pay**.
The key idea: each rate applies only to its own slice of the pay, and the tax credits come off the tax, not off the pay.
question: Ciara earns $€56\,000$ a year. She pays tax at $20\%$ on the first $€42\,000$ and $40\%$ on the rest. Her tax credits are $€3\,500$. Find her net pay.

title: Cost materials, labour and wastage
what: You give it a job: the amounts of materials, the price of each, the wastage and the labour. It gives back the **total cost**.
The key idea: cost each part of the job on its own, then add them. Wastage means buying more than you need, so the amount goes up by that percentage.
question: A room is $5$ m by $4$ m. The floor is to be tiled. Tiles cost $€30$ per m², and $8\%$ extra is bought for wastage. The tiler charges $€45$ per hour for $6$ hours. Find the total cost.

title: Calculate percentage error, tolerance and accumulated error
what: You give it an estimated value and the true value. It gives back the **percentage error**: how far off the estimate is, as a percentage of the truth.
The key idea: the error is the difference between the two values, and you always divide it by the **true** value.
question: A table is measured as $1.46$ m long. The true length is $1.50$ m. Find the percentage error, correct to one decimal place.

title: Calculate an average rate of change over time
what: You give it a change in some quantity and the time it took. It finds the **rate**: how much the quantity changes in each unit of time.
The key idea: rate is change divided by time. For a journey in parts, add up the total change and the total time first, then divide once.
question: A cyclist rides $18$ km in $45$ minutes, then $12$ km in $15$ minutes. Find her average speed for the whole journey, in km/h.

title: Find the present value of a future sum
what: You give it a future sum $F$, a yearly rate $i$ and a time $t$. It finds the amount $P$ you would have to invest **today** to reach $F$.
The key idea: compound interest multiplies by $(1+i)^t$, so going backwards means dividing by it.
question: How much should be invested today at $3.5\%$ per annum compound interest to have €8000 in $4$ years? Give your answer to the nearest cent.

title: Find the rate or time in a compound interest problem
output: i via roots, t via logs
what: You give it the start amount $P$, the final amount $F$, and either the time $t$ or the rate $i$. It finds the one that is missing.
The key idea: in $F = P(1+i)^t$, a **root** frees $i$ and a **log** frees $t$.
question: €20,000 is invested at $4\%$ per annum compound interest. After how many whole years will it first be worth at least €30,000?

title: Find the future value of regular savings
what: You give it a regular payment $A$, a rate $i$ for each period and the number of payments $n$. It finds what the savings are worth at the end.
The key idea: each payment grows for a different length of time, so the values form a **geometric series**. One sum formula adds them all.
question: Aoife saves €150 at the start of every month for $24$ months. The account pays $0.4\%$ compound interest per month. Find the value of her savings at the end of the $24$ months, to the nearest cent.

title: Find the present value of a series of payments (pension/annuity)
what: You give it a payment, a rate $i$ and a number of payments $n$. It gives back what the whole stream of payments is worth **today**.
The key idea: each payment is divided by $(1+i)$ once for every period it has to wait, and those present values form a **geometric series** you can add with one formula.
question: A pension pays €1500 at the end of each year for 6 years. The interest rate is 3% per year. Find the present value of the pension, correct to the nearest cent.
